heroHeading: Greece: Where the Aegean Defines Luxury
heroSubheading: The caldera at Oia holds the record for the most photographed sunset on earth — yet most visitors watch it shoulder to shoulder with strangers. Our clients watch it from a private terrace with chilled Assyrtiko, a personal chef behind them and a yacht below. Santorini and Mykonos together form the definitive Greek summer: one volcanic, contemplative, draped in white and blue; the other electric, cosmopolitan, alive until dawn. We handle every detail — transfers, villas, table reservations, sea access — so nothing interrupts the experience.

experiencesHeading: What to See and Do in Greece (Santorini & Mykonos)

experiences.title: Private Caldera Sunset Sail from Ammoudi Bay
experiences.body: Santorini's caldera is the flooded crater of one of history's most powerful volcanic eruptions — and from the water, its scale becomes visceral. We arrange a crewed private sailing yacht departing from the stone steps of Ammoudi Bay, circling the Red Beach and White Beach sea-cliffs before anchoring off the volcanic islet of Nea Kameni as the sky shifts through amber and violet. A private chef prepares fresh-caught sea bream and local mezze on board. The caldera walls rise three hundred metres above you. This is not a sunset cruise; it is a geology lesson filtered through the most beautiful light in the Mediterranean.
experiences.imageAlt: Private sailing yacht anchored in the Santorini caldera at golden hour

experiences.title: Exclusive Wine Tasting in Santorini's Ancient Assyrtiko Vineyards
experiences.body: Santorini's vines are among the oldest in the world — some root systems are believed to be over four centuries old, trained into basket shapes to protect the grapes from the fierce Aegean wind. The island's volcanic soil produces Assyrtiko with a mineral precision found nowhere else on earth. We arrange private after-hours access to estate cellars in the Pyrgos and Megalochori villages, where winemakers pour library vintages that never reach the open market. A sommelier guides the tasting; a private driver ensures you are returned safely to your villa. No tour groups, no time pressure.
experiences.imageAlt: Vineyard rows on volcanic Santorini soil at dusk with caldera view

experiences.title: Private Day Charter to the Beaches of Mykonos by Sea
experiences.body: The distance between Santorini and Mykonos is best covered as an experience in itself. We arrange a private motor yacht for the Aegean crossing — arriving at Psarou Beach or the quiet coves of Agios Sostis from the water, bypassing the port crowds entirely. On Mykonos, the best beach clubs hold tables exclusively; we confirm yours in advance. A snorkelling stop at the sea caves of Fokos Bay, lunch served on deck, and an afternoon at one of the island's legendary waterfront venues form a day that cannot be assembled from a booking website. Return by sunset or stay overnight — the itinerary is yours.
experiences.imageAlt: Mykonos windmills overlooking the blue Aegean waters on a clear summer day

experiences.title: Private Archaeology Session at Akrotiri, Santorini's Pompeii
experiences.body: Akrotiri is the buried Minoan city preserved beneath Santorini's volcanic ash since 1627 BC — older than Pompeii by fifteen centuries and still yielding its secrets. The site is ordinarily visited in large groups with little context. We arrange a private early-morning entry accompanied by an archaeologist who has worked the excavation personally. Walking the cobbled streets before the day's heat arrives, with no other visitors present and someone who can read the frescoes and street patterns as living history, transforms an archaeological site into an intimate encounter with a vanished civilisation. A light breakfast at a family-run kafeneion in nearby Akrotiri village follows.
experiences.imageAlt: Ancient ruins at Akrotiri archaeological site on Santorini island

experiences.title: Mykonos After Dark: Private Access to the Island's Best Evenings
experiences.body: Mykonos has been the social centre of the Mediterranean summer since the 1960s, and it remains so for a reason: the island understands how to construct an evening. The difficulty is that its best venues operate on invitation and relationship. We maintain those relationships on your behalf — securing tables at Scorpios before the waiting list opens, arranging a private room at Nammos for dinner ahead of the evening programme, and ensuring your transition between venues is seamless. A discreet driver is on call through the night. Whether your preference is a long dinner at a cliff-top terrace or dancing until the Aegean light returns, we prepare the evening entirely around you.
experiences.imageAlt: Mykonos town at night with illuminated whitewashed buildings and vibrant atmosphere

regions.name: Oia & the Northern Caldera, Santorini
regions.body: Oia occupies the northernmost tip of Santorini's crescent, clinging to the caldera rim above a three-hundred-metre drop to the sea. It is the island at its most concentrated: white-domed churches, cave houses carved directly into the volcanic rock, and that view. For our clients, Oia means a private villa with an infinity pool suspended over the caldera, a personal chef sourcing from the morning market, and mornings so quiet you can hear the water below. The village is best experienced before ten and after eight; we time your arrivals accordingly.
regions.imageAlt: Oia village on the Santorini caldera rim with iconic blue-domed churches at sunset

regions.name: Mykonos Town (Chora) & Little Venice
regions.body: Mykonos Town is the Cycladic village taken to its logical extreme — a labyrinth of whitewashed lanes designed to confuse pirates, now confusing only the happily lost. At its western edge, Little Venice is a row of medieval houses built directly over the sea, their balconies hanging above the water. In the afternoon, the light here is extraordinary. We arrange private walking tours with a local historian before the crowds arrive, hold dinner reservations at the waterfront restaurants that require weeks of notice, and ensure your villa in the hills above Chora is staffed and ready on arrival.
regions.imageAlt: Little Venice waterfront in Mykonos Town with colorful buildings over the Aegean

regions.name: Fira & the Caldera Villages, Santorini
regions.body: Fira is Santorini's capital and the island's commercial heart — but above the main thoroughfare, a network of caldera-edge paths connects it to the villages of Firostefani and Imerovigli with views that stop conversation mid-sentence. Imerovigli sits at the highest point of the caldera rim and offers the island's most unobstructed panorama. We position clients in private residences along this ridge path, with spa access, helicopter transfer options from Heraklion or Athens, and restaurant reservations at the small tables that face west. The walk between Fira and Oia at dawn — two hours, no crowds — is one of the Mediterranean's quiet masterpieces.
regions.imageAlt: Fira and Imerovigli caldera villages with white architecture and Aegean views

services.title: Private Villa Rental
services.body: We access Santorini and Mykonos villas that are not listed publicly — cave houses above the Oia caldera, estate compounds in Mykonos' Ano Mera hills, and cliff-side retreats with private infinity pools. faqsHeading: Frequently Asked Questions about Luxury Travel in Greece

faqs.question: How much does a private villa in Santorini or Mykonos cost per week?
faqs.answer: Private villa rentals in Santorini's Oia caldera and Mykonos' most sought-after locations typically range from €15,000 to €80,000 per week in peak season, depending on size, staff, and exclusivity of the property. Some off-market estates command higher rates. We present options matched to your requirements rather than a fixed catalogue, and negotiate directly with owners on your behalf.

faqs.question: What is the best time of year to visit Santorini and Mykonos for luxury travel?
faqs.answer: Late May through early June and September offer the ideal balance: warm Aegean temperatures, uncrowded caldera paths, and full availability of the best restaurants and beach clubs without the intensity of July and August. For yacht charters, this shoulder season also brings more favourable winds and easier berthing. July and August remain the most vibrant socially on Mykonos. We advise based on your priorities — privacy, nightlife, or sailing conditions.

faqs.question: Is it possible to rent a private island near Santorini or Mykonos?
faqs.answer: Several private islands and uninhabited islets in the Cyclades are accessible by yacht charter for a day or longer, offering complete seclusion. Full private island rentals in the Greek islands do exist but are rare and require significant advance planning. Our team maintains awareness of available properties and can arrange exclusive access to remote anchorages and beaches that effectively offer the privacy of a private island without the logistical complexity.

faqs.question: How do I get from Santorini to Mykonos privately?
faqs.answer: The most elegant option is a private motor yacht making the four-to-five-hour crossing, turning the transit into an experience. Alternatively, we arrange a short helicopter transfer — approximately forty minutes — or a direct private flight between the two island airports. Ferry crossings are available but not consistent with a private travel experience. We coordinate the inter-island movement as part of your full itinerary, ensuring timing aligns with villa check-ins and evening reservations.

faqs.question: Can Private Travel Club arrange last-minute bookings in Greece during peak season?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our relationships with villa owners, yacht operators and restaurant managers in Santorini and Mykonos allow us to move at speed when public availability shows nothing. We will not promise what we cannot deliver, but a significant portion of our Greek bookings are initiated with less than three weeks' notice. Contact us directly by WhatsApp or email and we assess availability honestly within hours.

faqs.question: What luxury experiences in Greece are genuinely exclusive and not available to the public?
faqs.answer: Private after-hours access to the Akrotiri archaeological site with a resident archaeologist, vineyard cellar tastings with library vintages not sold commercially, sunset anchorage in the caldera aboard a private crewed yacht, early-morning private tours of Oia before the village opens, and reserved sections at Mykonos beach clubs and nightlife venues that operate on personal introduction only. These are not add-ons — they are the substance of what we arrange.
